# Sāriputta Sutta (Snp 4.16 (PTS Snp 185))

**ID:** Snp 4.16 (PTS Snp 185)
**Section:** Suttanipāta (snp)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Sāriputta Sutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0505m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sāriputta Sutta* (Snp 4.16, verses 955–975), also titled *Therapañha Sutta* ("The Elder's Questions"), is the sixteenth and concluding discourse of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* in the *Suttanipāta* [Fronsdal 2016; Norman 1997-2001; Nyanaponika, Hecker, Bodhi 2003]. The text consists of an opening set of verses praising the Buddha followed by a series of questions posed by the venerable Sāriputta regarding the fears, hazards, and monastic training of a monk living in seclusion to eliminate mental defilements, together with the Buddha's corresponding replies [Fronsdal 2016; Nyanaponika, Hecker, Bodhi 2003].

The discourse is of notable historical and epigraphical interest, as it is widely identified with the *Upatisa-pasina* ("Upatissa's Question") recommended to monastics and laity by Emperor Aśoka in his third-century BCE Bhabru (Calcutta-Bairat) rock edict, Upatissa being Sāriputta's personal name [Bhattacharya 1948; Fronsdal 2016; Norman 1997-2001; Thomas 1933]. If this identification is accepted, it establishes that the sutta existed and was recognized as authoritative prior to 232 BCE [Fronsdal 2016].

Curated parallels include a passage-level Chinese parallel preserved in the *Arthapada Sūtra* (T 198) and a resembling passage in the Jain work *Isibhāsiyāiṁ* 38.6. The sutta is commented upon line-by-line in the canonical *Mahāniddesa* under the title *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), which interprets the opening verse as referring to the Buddha's descent from the Tāvatimsa heaven after preaching the Abhidhamma [Nyanaponika, Hecker, Bodhi 2003].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: T 198 佛說義足經
- Resembling parallels: Isibhāsiyāiṁ 38.6
- Mentioned in: Mnd 16 Sāriputtasuttaniddesa

**Sources**

- [Fronsdal 2016] Gil Fronsdal, Buddha before Buddhism: Wisdom from the Early Teachings (2016) — Information on Aśokan edicts, identification with Upatisa-pasine, and pre-232 BCE date.
- [Bhattacharya 1948] Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya, Buddhist Texts as Recommended by Asoka (1948) — Aśokan edict list equating Upatisapasina with Sāriputtasutta.
- [Nyanaponika, Hecker, Bodhi 2003] Nyanaponika Thera, Hellmuth Hecker, and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Great Disciples of the Buddha (2003) — Discussion of Therapañha Sutta, structure of questions and answers, and Mahāniddesa commentary.
- [Norman 1997-2001] K. R. Norman, The Group of Discourses (Sutta-Nipāta) (1997-2001) — Verse range (955-975), alternative title Therapañha-sutta, and note on Aśokan inscription.
- [Thomas 1933] Edward J. Thomas, The History of Buddhist Thought (1933) — Correlation between Aśoka's Upatisa-pasina and Sn 4.16.
